codeReview.summary: The consolidation is complete and correct. runtime_helpers.py (client building, volume state normalization, readiness polling, layout setup), snapshots.py (alist_snapshots, aget_snapshot, acreate_snapshot, aresolve_snapshot), and admin.py (_arun_admin_code) were all absorbed into runtime.py. wiki_bootstrap.py (568 lines, zero references) and its test file were deleted. runtime.py is now 1,302 lines but well-organized with 11 clear section headers (Daytona client building helpers, Volume state normalization, Volume readiness polling, Volume layout setup, Snapshot helpers, Admin process helpers, DaytonaSandboxRuntime, DaytonaSandboxSession, Session helpers, Public exports). The circular import between runtime.py and filesystem.py was broken by moving filesystem imports into the method bodies that need them (lines 1002-1007 and 1232-1236). All imports across the codebase were updated, including filesystem.py, diagnostics.py, and test files. Monkeypatch paths in test_runtime_snapshots.py, test_volumes.py, and test_runtime_diagnostics.py were updated to point at runtime.py.

issues.description: Redundant imports: both `import time` and `import time as _time` are present. `time` is used for `.time()` and `.perf_counter()`; `_time` is used for `.monotonic()`. This is harmless but could be simplified to a single `import time` and use `time.monotonic()` directly.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The circular import break pattern (local imports inside method bodies) used between runtime.py and filesystem.py is not documented in any shared state. This is a valid and necessary pattern when two modules in the same package have mutual runtime dependencies, but it would be helpful to document as a convention for future consolidation work.
